title: Consumer Relationship Exposure Cap — Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract
content:
Kestrel limits the total consumer credit it extends to one customer across products, and a Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract is funded only within that limit.

**Rule.** Relationship exposure is the sum of the principal balance on every open retail, pre-owned and balloon contract of the customer, plus the adjusted lease balance on every lease of the customer in active or maturity-extended status, plus the amount financed of the contract being booked. Relationship exposure must not exceed the relationship exposure cap of the tier being booked. When it would, the contract is not funded; there is no partial approval and no override at the servicing desk. Business customers' fleet units are commercial credit and never count toward consumer relationship exposure.

**Evidence.** The exposure is read from the company's own records of the customer's contracts and leases, together with the amount financed of the contract being booked; the cap is the figure for the tier the new contract is booked on.

### Components of relationship exposure

| Included | Measure taken |
|---|---|
| Open Kestrel retail, pre-owned and balloon contracts of the customer | principal balance |
| Kestrel leases of the customer in active or maturity-extended status | adjusted lease balance |
| The pre-owned contract being booked | amount financed |
| Fleet units of business customers | never included |

### Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

A customer holds an open retail contract with a principal balance of $14000.00 and an active lease with an adjusted lease balance of $21000.00, and asks to finance $18000.00 on a pre-owned contract. Exposure is $14000.00 plus $21000.00 plus $18000.00, that is $53000.00. Booked on a tier whose cap is $45000.00, the exposure exceeds the cap and the contract is not funded; neither a smaller approval nor a desk override is available. Booked on a tier whose cap is $65000.00, it is within the cap. All balances are illustrative.
